name: Hennig BEE-NET public structures and split files
description: Public structural subset and split metadata for BEE-NET, trained on DFT Eliashberg spectra reused from the Cerqueira superconductivity archive.
count_display: 5,241 CIF files; documented pool 4,192 train / 1,049 test
count_scope: Public Git structures plus split files; full target database and model checkpoints are explicitly not tracked

sources.title: BEE-NET immutable public file inventory
sources.evidence: Non-truncated public tree contains exactly 5241 CIFs and split indices; no database.json or licence file.

sources.title: BEE-NET author release documentation
sources.evidence: States 5241 entries, 1049 test and 4192 training-pool entries; database.json and model ensembles are not tracked; points to Cerqueira upstream.

sources.title: BEE-NET author preprint
sources.evidence: Training is ambient-pressure and Tc comparison uses DFT-derived Allen–Dynes values; high-pressure hydrides are outside its stated domain.

sources.title: BEE-NET journal paper
sources.evidence: Describes the AI-assisted discovery workflow; training-data availability points to BEE-NET GitHub.

caveats: Structure files and split metadata are open; a complete ready-to-train target database was not present in the public Git snapshot or GitHub Releases.
The 5241 entries are a curated subset of upstream calculations, not an independent set of newly computed or experimentally measured superconductors.
A large screened candidate pool and DFT-selected hits are different denominators from this training-structure release.
Two experimentally confirmed examples in the study do not convert all training labels into experimental Tc.
Ambient-pressure training and the stated 100 meV spectral ceiling limit use for high-pressure/high-frequency hydrides.
No data licence was located in the public repository.

additional_counts.scope: Author README, prior to bootstrap sampling; not additional structures
Author README and released test-ID file; included in 5241 total

name: Hennig–Xie Eliashberg / Allen–Dynes symbolic-regression benchmark
description: Public descriptor and Tc tables combining artificial spectra, computed material cases, literature hydrides and an Allen–Dynes comparison baseline.
count_display: 3,046 CSV rows across five tables; 3,017 excluding the 29-row comparison table
count_scope: Direct CSV count: artificial 2819 + calculated 30 + literature 149 + hydrides 19 + AD29 baseline 29; not unique materials

sources.title: Hennig–Xie Materials Cloud metadata
sources.evidence: Authors include Hennig and Xie; archive contains data_tables.zip plus SISSO records; rights metadata explicitly declares Apache-2.0.

sources.title: Hennig–Xie public numerical tables
sources.evidence: 429059-byte ZIP matches published MD5 86c68504d1780b6fc7eaccbd4116706c. Direct counts: AD29 29, artificial 2819, calculated 30, hydrides 19, literature 149.

sources.title: Xie et al. Eliashberg theory paper
sources.evidence: Separates 13 calculated, 29 classic and 13 hydride material spectra from 2819 artificial spectra; physical cases are resampled across mu*.

sources.title: Earlier Hennig–Xie analytical-form study (2019)
sources.evidence: Provides the prior Allen–Dynes-based formula context; no standalone 2018 data release was verified.

caveats: 3046 counts all public table rows, including an overlapping comparison baseline; it does not mean 3046 distinct crystals.
The primary spectral collection comprises 55 physical material cases plus 2819 artificial spectra; resampling mu* expands numerical rows.
Hydride validation has 13 material spectral functions / 19 table rows, not 19 unique hydride crystals.
Tables provide numerical theoretical targets and comparison values; no full CIF collection is deposited here.
Hydride pressures and full raw spectral inputs are not uniformly encoded in the public descriptor tables; consult original references. The paper says raw data are available upon request.
The 2019 analytical-form paper and the 2021 archive / 2022 successor paper are related; do not advertise an unverified separate 2018 release.

additional_counts.scope: Paper total: 55 physical cases plus 2819 artificial spectra; not all unique crystals
13 in-house calculated + 29 literature classic + 13 literature hydrides

name: Cerqueira–Sanna–Marques conventional-superconductor EPC archive
description: Open ground-state and electron–phonon calculations used upstream of Hennig BEE-NET, with structures, spectra and theoretical Tc estimates.
version: Materials Cloud 2023.163 v1; 2024 Advanced Materials paper
count_display: around 7,000 model-data calculations; paper reports >8,250 total EPC calculations
count_scope: Approximate model-data cohort described by archive; broader public batch archive includes additional calculations and was not enumerated

sources.title: Cerqueira EPC archive metadata
sources.evidence: Around 7000 electron–phonon calculations; 17 batch archives; rights metadata CC BY 4.0.

sources.title: Cerqueira EPC archive README
sources.evidence: Documents optimized CIF, alpha2F by smearing, phonon outputs and separate McMillan/Allen–Dynes and isotropic-Eliashberg Tc files.

sources.title: Sampling the Materials Space for Conventional Superconducting Compounds
sources.evidence: Paper distinguishes a broader total exceeding 8250 ab initio EPC calculations from ML screening over 191528 candidates.

caveats: Created by Cerqueira, Sanna and Marques, not the Hennig group; included because BEE-NET directly reuses a subset.
Do not sum the archive with the overlapping BEE-NET subset or parent Alexandria structures.
The approximate 7000 model-data figure and >8250 total calculations are distinct denominators; all raw archive records were not counted.
Tc values are computed conventional-superconductivity estimates, not experimental confirmations.
The reused BEE domain is ambient pressure; no pressure-resolved hydride benchmark is implied for all records.
